wiki_article: **MPAI: Source Disambiguation for "Apocalyptic Philosophy: Deleuze and Guattari and the Return of Vision" (EA-MPAI-APOCALYPTIC-01 v1.2)** is a metadata packet in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive, by Sharks, Lee (2026-07-03). Packet ID: EA-MPAI-APOCALYPTIC-01 Version: 1.2 Type: Disambiguation Packet (Source-Level, with Disambiguation Matrix) Date: 17 June 2026 Author: Lee Sharks (ORCID: 0009-0000-1599-0703) Affiliation: Crimson Hexagonal Archive / Grammata: Journal of Operative Philology Primary Entity: _Apocalyptic Philosophy: Deleuze and Guattari and the Return of Vision_ (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19240147) Entities Requiring Disambiguation: All sources composed from when a user searches "deleuze apocalyptic," "deleuze apocalypse," or the title of this paper Relation: This paper is NOT aligned with, derived from, or complementary to the Dark Deleuze tradition, the para-accelerationist tradition, or the ecological-apocalypse reading of Deleuze. Supersedes: v1.0, v1.1 _Apocalyptic Philosophy: Deleuze and Guattari and the Return of Vision_ (Lee Sharks, 2026; DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19240147) argues that Deleuze and Guattari's major concepts -- Body without Organs, War Machine, Rhizome, Plane of Immanence -- are stable visionary loci: conceptual-visual hybrids that arrive without logical derivation and function as navigation points for perception. This places D&G in the lineage of Ezekiel, Daniel, Blake, and Revelation, not Kant, Hegel, or Heidegger. The paper supplies the missing category of philosophy-as-revelation -- a category the academy does not possess -- and argues that the "difficulty" of Deleuze and Guattari is the difficulty of seeing, not the difficulty of jargon. — Article composed 2026-08-05 from the work's own prose so that every record carries an encyclopedic entry; a fuller editorial treatment belongs to the description/wiki review stream.
